@@ -78,6 +78,128 @@ All detected secrets are replaced with `REDACTED`. PII matches are replaced with
 
 To reduce over-redaction, Entire preserves structural transcript fields such as IDs and paths, leaves placeholder values alone, and redacts only credential values for bounded key/value forms. Placeholders are detected by exact match (e.g. `changeme`, `example`, `placeholder`, `your_password`, `your_secret`, prior `REDACTED`/`[REDACTED]`/`<REDACTED>` markers) or by shape: shell expansions like `${DB_PASSWORD}`, bracketed names like `<password>` or `<your-db-password>`, and mask runs of three or more `*`/`x`/`.`/`-` (so `***`, `xxxx`, `....`, `----` all match). When a connection string contains a real password, it is redacted as a unit because partial fragments can still expose sensitive material; connection strings whose passwords are placeholders are left intact.
 
+## Customizing redaction
+
+The built-in detectors handle well-known secret formats. For anything else you don't want stored in transcripts — internal credential shapes the bundled scanners don't know about, project codenames, or specific words and phrases you'd rather keep out of session archives — Entire offers two extension surfaces. Both run plain regex matching against transcript content, so the rules can target any string pattern, not just credentials. Both feed the same engine and run as their own layer between connection-string detection and bounded credential KV detection.
+
+### Surface 1: Inline `redaction.custom_redactions`
+
+Add a label → regex map under `redaction.custom_redactions` in `.entire/settings.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "redaction": {
+    "custom_redactions": {
+      "acme_token":  "ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}",
+      "internal_id": "INTERNAL_[a-z]{6}_[0-9]{4}"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+- The label is for diagnostics only; matches are replaced with the bare `REDACTED` token (matching the built-in secret layers, not the `[REDACTED_<LABEL>]` token used for PII).
+- Regexes follow [Go's RE2 syntax](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/syntax). No lookarounds, no backreferences.
+- A failed compile is logged once at startup and the rule is skipped — it will never crash the redactor.
+- Override in `.entire/settings.local.json` for personal additions; entries merge per-key (override replaces the same key, leaves other keys intact).
+
+### Surface 2: Rule packs
+
+Drop a YAML or JSON file into `.entire/redactors/`:
+
+```yaml
+# .entire/redactors/acme-internal.yaml
+name: acme-internal              # MUST match the filename stem
+version: 1.0.0
+description: Internal ACME service tokens
+rules:
+  - id: acme-token
+    description: Long-lived ACME service tokens
+    regex: 'ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'
+    samples:
+      - { input: "REDACTED", redacted: true  }
+      - { input: "ACME_TOKEN_short",                     redacted: false }
+  - id: acme-session
+    regex: 'asess_[a-f0-9]{32}'
+```
+
+Equivalent JSON form:
+
+```json
+{
+  "name": "acme-internal",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "rules": [
+    {
+      "id": "acme-token",
+      "regex": "ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}",
+      "samples": [
+        { "input": "REDACTED", "redacted": true  },
+        { "input": "ACME_TOKEN_short",                     "redacted": false }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+**Required fields:** `name` (must equal the filename stem — `acme-internal.yaml` → `acme-internal`), `version` (any string; semver recommended), and `rules[]` (at least one entry, each with `id` and `regex`).
+
+**Optional fields:** `description` (pack-level and rule-level), and `rules[].samples[]` (see "Self-tests" below).
+
+A pack does not have to target credentials. The same shape works for any string pattern you don't want stored in transcripts — for example, a project codename or a small word list:
+
+```yaml
+# .entire/redactors/local/private-words.yaml
+name: private-words
+version: 1.0.0
+description: Project codenames and personal words to keep out of transcripts
+rules:
+  - id: codename-falcon
+    description: Internal project codename
+    regex: '(?i)\bproject[- ]?falcon\b'
+    samples:
+      - { input: "rolling out Project Falcon next week", redacted: true  }
+      - { input: "the falcon flew over",                  redacted: false }
+  - id: personal-words
+    description: Words I'd rather not see archived
+    regex: '(?i)\b(word_one|word_two)\b'
+```
+
+Putting personal lists under `.entire/redactors/local/` keeps them out of team commits (see "Distribution" below).
+
+### Self-tests via `samples[]`
+
+Each rule may declare an array of `{input, redacted}` pairs. On the next process startup after editing the pack, Entire runs each sample and emits a `slog.Warn` for any mismatch:
+
+```
+WARN  redactor pack sample mismatch  pack=.entire/redactors/acme-internal.yaml
+      rule=acme-token sample_index=0 sample_length=42 expected=true got=false
+```
+
+A failing sample never disables the rule — sample validation is informational. Use it to catch typos and false positives before they ship.
+
+### Distribution
+
+- **Within a team:** commit `.entire/settings.json` and/or `.entire/redactors/*` to your repo. Teammates pull and the rules apply.
+- **Across teams:** copy the pack file or share a link to a gist; recipients drop the file into their `.entire/redactors/`.
+- **Personal-only:** put the file in `.entire/redactors/local/` — `entire enable` writes that path into `.entire/.gitignore` so personal rules don't pollute team commits.
+
+### When to write a rule vs. file an issue
+
+Write a rule for:
+
+- Internal service tokens (`ACME_*`, `INTERNAL_*`) and custom env-var prefixes the bundled detectors don't know about.
+- Project-specific session formats.
+- Project codenames or other identifiers you don't want stored in transcripts.
+- Specific words or phrases you'd rather keep out of session archives.
+
+File an issue when the rule would benefit every Entire user (e.g., a major SaaS issued a new token format), when a built-in is producing false positives on common idioms in your codebase, or when a built-in is *not* catching a well-known shared format (we'd rather fix the built-in than have everyone ship the same custom rule).
+
+### Troubleshooting
+
+- **My rule doesn't redact anything.** Warnings about invalid patterns or sample mismatches appear on stderr when Entire initializes redaction, such as hooks that write checkpoints or `entire doctor`. Look for lines mentioning your label or pack path.
+- **My pack file is silently ignored.** Filenames must end in `.yaml`, `.yml`, or `.json`. Other extensions are skipped.
+- **I want to disable a rule temporarily.** Comment it out (prefix the YAML key with `#`) or remove the entry from `custom_redactions`. The rule reloads on the next CLI invocation.
+
 ## Limitations
 
 - **Best-effort.** Novel or low-entropy secrets (short passwords, predictable tokens) may not be caught.

Looking over PR #1076 "Add user-defined redaction rules and rule packs" (currently REVIEW_REQUIRED, all CI green).

## Verdict

Looks good to ship. Architecture is clean, error paths are warn-and-skip (right call for a security feature — one bad rule shouldn't silence the rest), and test coverage is thorough. A few comments below — none are blockers.

## Strengths

- **Two surfaces, one engine.** Inline `custom_redactions` and pack files feed the same compiled-rule list; the layered split in `redact.String()` is a one-liner add (layer 5) — minimal risk to existing detectors.
- **Warn-and-skip across the board.** Invalid regex, missing dir, unreadable file, symlink, schema error, sample mismatch — none are fatal. The settings-load and pack-walk paths cannot kill redaction.
- **Strict schema parsing.** `DisallowUnknownFields` on JSON, `KnownFields(true)` on YAML, *and* an extra `Decode(&extra)` to reject trailing content / multi-doc YAML. Good belt-and-suspenders.
- **Per-key local override semantics** (`mergeRedaction`) are correct and tested at the merge layer (`TestLoadMerged_CustomRedactionsPerKeyOverride`).
- **`redactors/local/`** convention + `.entire/.gitignore` integration is a nice UX touch for personal rules.
- **Privacy-aware logging.** `REDACTED` is a great regression guard — sample inputs are summarized by `sample_index` + `sample_length`, never raw.

## Things worth a second look

1. **`paths.AbsPath` failure fallback walks CWD** — `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:380-386`. If `WorktreeRoot` fails (e.g., process started outside a repo, but settings somehow loaded), `packsDir` falls back to the relative `.entire/redactors`. `LoadPacks` then walks that path relative to CWD, which can pick up an unrelated `.entire/redactors/` if someone happened to be in a directory that has one. Low likelihood, but the safer move is to skip pack-loading entirely on `paths.AbsPath` failure. Optional.

2. **No guard against over-broad regex (e.g. `.*`, `(.+)`).** A user-supplied `.*` would redact every transcript. Sample-validation catches this only if they wrote samples. Consider either (a) a doc warning under "Customizing redaction" that an unanchored permissive regex will eat everything, or (b) rejecting patterns that match the empty string at compile time. Doc fix is enough IMO.

3. **No de-duplication across packs.** `validatePack` rejects duplicate rule IDs *within* a pack, but two packs can both define `id: api-key`. Behavior is correct (both run, both labels stay distinct via `pack.Name+"."+rule.ID`), but if two packs happen to have the same `name` (e.g., one in root + one in `local/`), the labels collide in logs. Worth a one-liner check in `LoadPacks` to warn on duplicate pack names, or just document it.

4. **Filename-stem-must-match-pack-name** is enforced (`packs.go:107`). Justification is good (consistent logs/discovery), but it's a UX papercut on rename and isn't documented in `docs/security-and-privacy.md`. Add one line to the "Required fields" section: "`name` must equal the filename stem (e.g., `acme-internal.yaml` → `acme-internal`)" — actually you already have this. Nevermind, good.

5. **Per-call linear scan.** `detectCustomRules` runs `FindAllStringIndex` per rule per `String()` call. Fine for tens of rules; with hundreds of pack rules and high-frequency transcript scanning, worth keeping in mind. Not a today-problem.

6. **Minor test gap:** symlinked *subdirectory* (vs. symlinked file) isn't covered. `WalkDir` won't follow them by default, and `d.Type()&fs.ModeSymlink` will skip them, but a one-line test would lock the behavior in.

7. **`Pack.Description` / `Rule.Description`** are accepted by the schema but never surfaced anywhere (no logs, no `entire doctor`). Fine to keep as human-readability fields, but a comment to that effect on the struct would prevent "why isn't this shown?" issues later.

## Nits

- `EnsureRedactionConfigured` is wrapped in `sync.Once`, which means rule edits require a process restart. That's the right model, but it's not in the docs — worth one line under "Troubleshooting" ("rule changes take effect on the next CLI invocation"). You already have something close ("The rule reloads on the next CLI invocation") under "disable a rule temporarily" — maybe make it general.
- `redact/custom.go:25` — `label` on `compiledCustomRule` is never read at redact time (regions are emitted with empty label). Comment already says this; could simplify by dropping the field entirely and only keeping it in log-emission scope. Cosmetic.

Happy to push fixes for any of these if you want — say the word.

Branch is now 5 commits ahead of origin, lint and tests clean.

**Summary of `10f1f52fc`:**

The fix is one-place: `logging.Init` now calls `slog.SetDefault(logger)` on every path (file-backed and both stderr fallbacks). `Close` and `resetLogger` swap `slog.Default()` back to a fresh stderr-backed JSON handler *before* tearing down the buffered file writer, so any post-Close bare `slog.*` call has a safe destination instead of trying to write to a closed file.

Why this place instead of refactoring `redact/` to take an injected logger:
- One change covers redact custom.go, packs.go, **and pii.go** (which had the same bug latent — its invalid-pattern warning never made it to the log either).
- Future leaf packages that use bare slog inherit the fix.
- The redact package stays as a leaf with zero CLI dependencies.

Tradeoff: bare slog calls from `redact/` don't carry the per-call session_id / tool_call_id context that `logging.Warn(ctx, …)` decorates messages with. They get the right destination and the right `component=redaction` attr — enough to `grep` for in entire.log — but not the session breadcrumbs. If you want those too, the follow-up is a `redact.SetLogger(*slog.Logger)` injection from the strategy layer; happy to do that as a separate commit. Otherwise this resolves the misleading-docs/breadcrumb concern.
